messages:
Maya: seeing a bunch of customer reports where response_format=json + strict=true fails intermittently during traffic spikes. They get a 500 or a 422 with "invalid JSON" even though model output looks fine upstream.
Alex: can you paste the exact curl you used + raw response?
Maya: here — repro from a customer: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-8b","response_format":"json","strict":true,"input":"summarize: ..."}'
```
Maya: response (truncated):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=--xyz
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

----xyz
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"choices":[{"text":"Summary..."}]}
----xyz
Content-Type: text/plain

Warning: truncated
----xyz--
```
Jordan: ah — upstream is emitting multipart boundaries when we stream tool outputs for the model. Our parser expects a single JSON document (and strict=true rejects anything else). If the server interleaves a text part for warnings, strict parsing fails.
Alex: that would explain the 422 when the client sees non-JSON top-level. But why the 500s?
Sam: found an error in runtime logs during surge: `jsonmode-parser: Unexpected MIME part sequence` and then `panic: write after response finished` causing a 500. Looks correlated with CPU saturation during burst.
InfraBot: incident created #INC-2026-73 — routing to eng-runtime, priority P2.
Maya: customer hit this on Friday at 14:12 UTC — burst from 120->900 rps, tenant on Dedicated. Billing shows normal usage, so not a quota throttle.
Jordan: reproduction steps I ran locally: run loader at 400 rps w/ response_format=json + strict true. After ~6 min some responses returned `Content-Type: multipart/mixed` and the client failed parsing.
Jordan: quick workaround for customers: set `strict=false` or add `Accept: application/json; profile=redwood-structured` (we have a negotiated path that prefers single-part JSON). Not ideal.
Alex: proposed fixes: 1) make parser tolerant of a single JSON part then ignore trailing text parts when strict=true if they are `text/plain` warnings; 2) ensure runtime serializes as `application/json` for structured outputs even during streaming; 3) add backpressure to avoid the panic under CPU pressure.
Maya: customer asked for hotfix or config toggle they can enable immediately.
Jordan: I can push a small parser patch to tolerate trailing text parts (failsafe) — will require tests. Risk low. But the 500 'panic' needs SRE + eng-runtime patch for the race.
Alex: escalate to eng-runtime for the panic (P1 for availability) and eng-ml for model-side multipart emission (P2). Sam, can you attach the relevant logs and stack traces?
Sam: attaching minimal log snippet: 
```
2026-03-13T14:12:05Z runtime: stream part boundary received
2026-03-13T14:12:05Z runtime: emit json part
2026-03-13T14:12:06Z runtime: jsonmode-parser: Unexpected MIME part sequence
2026-03-13T14:12:06Z runtime: panic: write after response finished
goroutine 112 [running]:
net/http.(*conn).serve.func1(0x0)

```
Sam: also saw a handful of 502s from upstream in the same window but not consistent.
Maya: customer note: they set `Accept: application/json` and `response_format=json` expecting strict behavior — this regression broke their production. They want ETA and temporary mitigation.
Jordan: temporary mitigation options to propose: A) tell customers to set `strict=false` (low effort) B) set `Accept: application/json; profile=redwood-structured` (we'll honor this to force single JSON) C) rate-limit bursts from tenant (ugh).
Alex: I'll notify customer success with those options and offer to enable profile flag for them while we patch.
Maya: CS notified and requested a timeline.
InfraBot: @eng-runtime-tag PING — incident INC-2026-73 assigned.
Jordan: draft PR that strips `text/*` parts and keeps first `application/json` part when `strict=true` — will run unit tests and a 1k-rps soak. ETA ~6h for PR, 24-48h for rollout. The panic fix will need SRE pairing — ETA TBD.
Alex: thanks. add postmortem later if we hit SLA. For now mark this P2 for customer impact but P1 for runtime panic.
Maya: customer appreciates quick workaround — please post updates here as you have them. :thumbsup:
